title: Opuscula cum Vita
shelf_note: Pico's collected works (Bologna 1496/98), with the Apologia and the Oration, the founding texts of Christian Kabbalah.
structure_note: 303 records, all with OCR and translation, no printed numbers captured. Nothing structural stands out. The defects are per-page OCR failures (reasoning dump, truncation, a macron loop), and those pages still have a fluent English translation.

book_verdict: Two of four pages are broken: one holds model reasoning instead of OCR and one a macron loop, and both carry fluent English that is not on the page (one of them is a false Kabbalah passage in the Oration). Page 165 drops three quarters of its text. The sound page (18) is good.
reader_summary: This is the 1496/98 Bologna collected works of Pico, with the Life, the Apologia and the Oration. Where the transcription exists it is of the right text and the English is close. On two of four sampled pages the transcription failed, and the English shown is invented, including a passage on Kabbalah that the page does not contain, so the English cannot be trusted page by page.

title: Doctissimi Viri Ioannis Pici Mirandulae, Concordiae comitis: Exactissima expositio in orationem dominicam
shelf_note: Pico is central to Latin Kabbalah, but this is a devotional exposition of the Lord's Prayer with no Kabbalistic content on the sampled pages; it fits by author only.
structure_note: 34 records, all OCR'd and translated. Pages 6–25 used gemini-3-flash OCR and page 29 used flash-lite (pipeline_preview), with a different expansion convention (bracketed 'igit[ur]'). No structural break.

other.note: the OCR's scan warning appears in the reader's English as '<note>Minor ink bleed-through from the preceding page is visible on the left margin.</note>'

tr_errors.problem: 'illud virginis' is the Virgin's saying (the Magnificat) fulfilled, not something fulfilled for her

ocr_errors.image: Q m āt refici (Quoniam autem refici)

ocr_errors.problem: bracketed expansions here, but the other pages keep the abbreviation marks; the convention flips within the book

tr_errors.english: Like the custom of one who is ill: who, when he has been healed, asks the doctor to give him some medicine or a way of life, so that he may preserve his health.
tr_errors.problem: the page ends at 'q vbi sana'; the rest of the sentence is supplied from the next page or invented

book_verdict: Clean, faithful transcription and English on all four pages, with small slips: a show-through margin note, a Magnificat line mistranslated, and a sentence completed past the page end. Its place on a Kabbalah shelf is by author only.
reader_summary: A 1537 printing of Pico's exposition of the Lord's Prayer, a devotional commentary on pride, the love of God and the daily bread. The transcription is of the right text and close to the print, and the English is faithful with minor slips. It contains no Kabbalah, so a reader looking for that will not find it here.

title: Artis cabalisticae. Tomus I
shelf_note: Pistorius's 1587 Basel anthology: Ricius, Leone Ebreo, Reuchlin's De arte cabalistica and De verbo mirifico. This is the core corpus of Christian Kabbalah.
structure_note: 1136 records against a pages_count field of 1120 and pages_translated field of 1114, so the counters are stale. 72 printed backsteps and 116 repeats among 1072 numbered pages is a lot. Some will be misread numerals and some split-spread artefacts (most sampled images are crops). I cannot tell which from four pages. The sampled leaves are in order (printed 113, 381, 676, 962).

book_verdict: Sound throughout the sample: four pages from Ricius, Leone Ebreo and Reuchlin read close to the print, with careful, faithful English. The only slips are one eye-skipped sentence and one invented heading. The page counters disagree with the records.
reader_summary: Volume I of Pistorius's Artis cabalisticae (Basel 1587), the standard Renaissance anthology of Christian Kabbalah: Ricius's De coelesti agricultura, Leone Ebreo's Dialogues, and Reuchlin's De arte cabalistica and De verbo mirifico. The transcription is of the right text and very close to the print, Greek included. The English is faithful and its notes are accurate. One sampled page drops a sentence.

title: [Vocabularius breviloquus]
shelf_note: A medieval Latin dictionary (Basel 1478), traditionally ascribed to Reuchlin. It is a lexicon, not Kabbalah, and belongs on a reference or lexicography shelf.
structure_note: On all four sampled pages the transcription is the text of the PRECEDING leaf. OCR 103 ends at 'Cardularij ... sic tradit' and image 103 opens 'in glo.l.i.ff.de iudi.'. OCR 323 ends at 'Nitru ... minuto' and image 323 opens 'sabulo'. The same holds for 381 ('precatrix' / 'Et pd.pe.') and 583 ('maturat h. qsi' / 'cū maturitate'). This is a book-wide one-leaf offset between images and text, not a misread numeral. 13 of 668 pages are untranslated.

book_verdict: Wrong shelf, and broken: on every sampled page the text and English belong to the preceding leaf, which points to a book-wide one-leaf offset. The OCR of the incunable's abbreviations is also rough.
reader_summary: This is the Vocabularius breviloquus, a 1478 Latin dictionary ascribed to Reuchlin, not a Kabbalistic work. On every page sampled the transcription and English belong to the leaf before the one shown. The headword readings are themselves often garbled, so neither the text nor the English can be used as it stands.
